outcome: No result since 26 January 2024 addresses the p=1 (L1/rectilinear) case stated in this bullet; the case n<=4 remains the only proven range and the O(n log n) general upper bound (Konyagin, pre-2024) is unchanged. A wave of 2026 papers resolved the analogous conjecture for p>1, but every one of them explicitly excludes or is silent on p=1.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet states Kusner's conjecture specifically for L1 (p=1) spaces: at most 2d points can be equidistant in d-dimensional L1. This is a distinct sub-case of the general Kusner conjecture, which asks for the maximum equilateral-set cardinality in l_p^n for every 1<p<infinity (conjectured n+1 for 1<p<infinity, and separately 2n for p=1). Since January 2024 there has been substantial activity on the general conjecture for p>1: Ge, Xu and Zhou ('Kusner's conjecture: Exact values and linear bounds,' arXiv:2606.03987, June 2026) proved the conjecture for 2<=p<=4 and gave near-linear O_p(n log n) bounds on complementary ranges of p; a follow-up (arXiv:2608.14013 and arXiv:2609.14794, August/September 2026) produced explicit counterexamples disproving the conjecture for p>4, building on Swanepoel's earlier (pre-2024) disproof for 1<p<2. Combined, this settles the p>1 range of the general Kusner conjecture. However, I read past the abstracts into the introductions of arXiv:2606.03987 (both the abs page rendering and the full HTML), and both explicitly restrict their theorems to p>=2 (or p in [2,4] and adjacent ranges), stating that for p=1 the conjecture 'holds for n<=4, with the cases n=3 and n=4 established by Bandelt, Chepoi and Laurent, and by Koolen, Laurent and Schrijver' (all pre-2024, decades-old results), and that the best known general bound for p=1 remains Konyagin's O(n log n), also pre-2024. None of the three 2026 papers found by triage, nor the current Wikipedia 'Equilateral dimension' article (which cites nothing past 2008), nor any further search I ran, turned up a paper that narrows, proves, or disproves the p=1 case specifically. The p>1 resolution is a related/parallel problem in the sense of this dataset's scope rule (§3.1): it changes the l_p conjecture for p>1, but the bullet in front of me is exactly the p=1 case, which those papers deliberately carve out and leave untouched. So the correct classification is 'open' with no_change_found true, agreeing with the triage's 'none' verdict. No AI system appears anywhere in this research trail: all three papers are ordinary human-authored combinatorial/discrete-geometry proofs with no stated model involvement of any kind.
competing_reading: One could argue the general Kusner conjecture (as a single named conjecture across all p, including p=1) has now been 'mostly resolved' and treat the p=1 sub-case as inheriting some evidentiary momentum, especially since the same authors (Ge, Xu, Zhou) explicitly handle p=1 as part of their conjecture statement (citing the n<=4 cases as already known). But the paper's own theorems and bounds sections give it no new treatment; the p=1 case is recited as background, not advanced. I do not think this rises to 'progress' under the letter of the rule, since nothing about what a careful reader would write in the p=1 bullet has changed.
what_would_settle_it: A paper explicitly proving or disproving Kusner's conjecture for p=1 in some dimension n=5 or higher (beyond the pre-2024 n<=4 results), or improving the O(n log n) bound for p=1 specifically, would move this out of 'open'.
